limitations: An original, simplified teaching model generated from code, not from medical imaging. Shapes, wall thickness and proportions are approximate; chambers are shown as solid forms rather than hollow muscle, and small vessels, cardiac veins and trabeculae are omitted. Colours follow the teaching convention (blue for oxygen-poor blood). Not for diagnosis or clinical use. Explanations drafted by Apex from the listed general references; not yet reviewed by an engineer or clinician.

parts.name: Left ventricle
parts.purpose: The main pumping chamber: its thick wall pushes oxygen-rich blood out through the aorta to the whole body.
parts.connection: Fills from the left atrium through the mitral valve; empties through the aortic valve. Forms the apex, the pointed tip.
parts.model_note: Shown as a solid form; real ventricles are hollow with thick muscular walls.

parts.name: Right ventricle
parts.purpose: Pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs. It needs far less pressure than the left, so its wall is thinner.
parts.connection: Fills from the right atrium through the tricuspid valve; empties through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
parts.model_note: Shown as a solid form wrapped against the left ventricle.

parts.name: Right atrium
parts.purpose: Receives oxygen-poor blood returning from the body.
parts.connection: Fed by the superior and inferior venae cavae; passes blood to the right ventricle. Home of the sinoatrial node, the natural pacemaker.

parts.name: Left atrium
parts.purpose: Receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs.
parts.connection: Fed by the four pulmonary veins; passes blood to the left ventricle through the mitral valve.

parts.name: Interventricular septum
parts.purpose: The muscular wall between the ventricles, keeping oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood apart.
parts.connection: Shared by both ventricles; the conduction bundle branches run down each side of it.

parts.name: Aorta
parts.purpose: The largest artery: carries oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle to the body.
parts.connection: Rises from the aortic valve, arches over the pulmonary arteries, gives off the head and arm arteries, and descends behind the heart.

parts.name: Pulmonary trunk & arteries
parts.purpose: Carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. The only arteries that carry oxygen-poor blood.
parts.connection: Splits into the left and right pulmonary arteries, the right one passing under the aortic arch.

parts.name: Superior vena cava
parts.purpose: Returns oxygen-poor blood from the head, neck and arms.
parts.connection: Enters the top of the right atrium.

parts.name: Inferior vena cava
parts.purpose: Returns oxygen-poor blood from the lower body.
parts.connection: Enters the bottom of the right atrium.

parts.name: Pulmonary veins
parts.purpose: Bring oxygen-rich blood back from the lungs, two from each lung.
parts.connection: Enter the back of the left atrium.

parts.name: Tricuspid valve
parts.purpose: Three leaflets that let blood pass from the right atrium into the right ventricle and stop it flowing back.
parts.connection: Tethered by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles in the ventricle, which stop the leaflets turning inside out.

parts.name: Mitral valve
parts.purpose: Two leaflets between the left atrium and left ventricle; closes when the ventricle contracts.
parts.connection: Tethered by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles in the left ventricle.

parts.name: Aortic valve
parts.purpose: Three pocket-like cusps at the exit of the left ventricle that stop blood falling back from the aorta.
parts.connection: At the root of the aorta; the coronary arteries branch off just above it.

parts.name: Pulmonary valve
parts.purpose: Three cusps at the exit of the right ventricle that stop blood falling back from the pulmonary trunk.
parts.connection: At the root of the pulmonary trunk.

parts.name: Coronary arteries
parts.purpose: The heart muscle's own blood supply. A blockage here causes a heart attack.
parts.connection: Branch from the base of the aorta and run in the grooves on the surface: left anterior descending, circumflex and right coronary artery.

parts.name: Electrical conduction system
parts.purpose: The electrical wiring that times each beat: SA node, AV node, bundle of His and bundle branches.
parts.connection: Starts at the SA node in the right atrium, pauses at the AV node, then runs down the septum to spread through both ventricles.
parts.model_note: Shown glowing and simplified; really microscopic tissue within the walls.
